deep.reconstruction:
Setting: k is a commutative ring, and P, Q are small k-linear (k-additive) categories. Grothendieck writes C^& = Hom_k(C°, Ab_k), the category of k-linear presheaves (right C-modules). He calls such a category, or one equivalent to it, an 'algebraic k-additive topos'. Ab_k is the category of k-modules.

(1) The tensor product P⊗_k Q has as objects pairs (a,b) and as morphisms Hom(a,a')⊗_k Hom(b,b'). Up to additive completion it embeds in its presheaf category. That presheaf category is identified with k-bilinear functors P°×Q°→Ab_k. On objects the embedding (*) sends a⊗b to (x,y) ↦ Hom_P(x,a)⊗_k Hom_Q(y,b), the external tensor product of representables h_a⊠h_b. By enriched Yoneda this is fully faithful. So a concrete model of P⊗_k Q, as an additive category, is the full subcategory of Bil_k(P°,Q°;Ab_k) consisting of finite sums of such functors.

(2) Application 1. Let M ≃ Q^& and let M^∨ ≃ Q°^& be 'the' dual (well defined up to equivalence, hence the quotes). Then P^&_M, the k-linear P-modules with values in M, is Hom_k(P°, Hom_k(Q°,Ab_k)). By currying this is Hom_k(P°⊗Q°, Ab_k) = (P⊗Q)^&. Dually, P°^&_{M^∨} ≃ Hom(P⊗Q, Ab_k) = (P⊗Q)°^&. Both are again algebraic k-additive topoi, since P⊗Q exists and is small (marginal note), and they are dual to each other.

(3) Application 2. Cocontinuous-in-each-variable bilinear functors P^&×Q^&→M are equivalent to cocontinuous linear functors (P⊗Q)^&→M. These in turn are equivalent to Bil_k(P,Q;M) when M is k-additive and cocomplete. So (P⊗_k Q)^& is the tensor product of the k-additive topoi P^&, Q^& inside k-linear categories stable under colimits.

Purpose: build a 2-categorical 'tensor calculus' for additive/abelian topoi (module categories) as part of the 'Abelianization' project. These are additive analogues of topoi, with duality M ↔ M^∨ and tensor products.
errors: Small gap in (1): the image of P⊗_k Q is just the representables h_a⊠h_b. 'Finite sums' give its additive envelope. The model is therefore of the tensor product in the 2-category of additive categories, which Grothendieck does indicate with ':= la cat. add. pleine correspondante'.
The phrase 'en dualité' is asserted, not proved here. The duality (Mod A dual to Mod A°, with evaluation and coevaluation given by A as a bimodule) is correct, but no argument is given on the page.
'Le' dual depends on M only through the Cauchy/Karoubi completion of Q. This is fine, but it is left implicit (only the quotation marks hint at it).

ideas.what: Tensor product of small k-linear categories, realized through the Yoneda embedding as sums of external products of representables inside bilinear functors
ideas.modern_name: Tensor product of enriched (Ab_k-)categories / ringoids; Yoneda embedding for P⊗Q
ideas.usually_credited_to: Eilenberg–Kelly (1966), Kelly 'Basic Concepts of Enriched Category Theory' (1982), Mitchell 'Rings with several objects' (1972)

ideas.what: Mod(P) with values in Mod(Q) equals Mod(P⊗Q) (currying)
ideas.modern_name: Enriched currying / exponential law for functor categories

ideas.what: Duality of algebraic k-additive topoi: Mod(Q) and Mod(Q°) are mutually dual, compatibly with tensor products
ideas.modern_name: Dualizability of module categories in the symmetric monoidal 2-category of presentable/cocomplete k-linear categories (Morita/Cauchy duality)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Morita theory; Street, Kelly (Cauchy completion, 1980s); modern form in Lurie HA §4.6 and Ben-Zvi–Francis–Nadler (2010)

ideas.what: (P⊗Q)^& is the universal recipient of separately cocontinuous bilinear functors from P^&×Q^&
ideas.modern_name: Kelly tensor product of cocomplete linear categories; Mod(A)⊠Mod(B)=Mod(A⊗B) (Deligne-type tensor product for module categories)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Kelly (1982, tensor products of cocomplete categories / Day convolution); Deligne 'Catégories tannakiennes' (1990) for abelian categories; López Franco (2013)

missed.claim: Around 1982, independently of Kelly/Street, Grothendieck sets up a symmetric monoidal 2-category of 'algebraic k-additive topoi' (module categories over small k-linear categories). It has a dual M^∨ and a tensor product characterized by separately cocontinuous bilinear functors. Together this is essentially the presentable/Morita 2-category in which module categories are dualizable. It is a historical precursor of the Deligne/Kelly tensor product and of Ben-Zvi–Francis–Nadler-style dualizability, inside his 'Abelianization' project. Mathematically it is standard today.
missed.quote: i.e. (P⊗_kQ)^& joue le rôle du produit tensoriel des topos k-additifs P^&, Q^&, parmi les cat. k-additives stables par lim
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical. It documents that Grothendieck's additive-topos program included a dualizable tensor calculus of module categories, predating Deligne 1990. It does not add new mathematics.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is clean, correct enriched category theory: tensor product of ringoids, Mod(P)⊗Mod(Q)=Mod(P⊗Q), and duality Mod Q ↔ Mod Q°. It was known or rediscovered by Kelly, Street, Deligne and others. Its interest is historical: Grothendieck's framing as a theory of 'k-additive topoi' with duality.
transcription_corrections: 'stables par lim' and 'avec lim': the limit is almost certainly the inductive limit (lim with right arrow, i.e. colimits), matching the subscripts k! and k!! for cocontinuous functors.
The struck-out symbol before 'Hom_{k!}' in Appl. 2 is a deleted abbreviation; the intended statement is Bil_{k!!}(P^&,Q^&;M) ≃ Hom_{k!}((P⊗_kQ)^&, M).
In (*) the formula is Hom_P(x,a)⊗_k Hom_Q(y,b); the image reads 'Hom_P(x,−)' loosely, but the variable is a.
